Il carcinoma epatocellulare nasce quasi:
Hepatocellular carcinoma almost always arises in a cirrhotic liver or one with chronic liver disease (hepatitis B or C, alcohol, steatohepatitis). Histologically: trabeculae thicker than 2-3 cells, loss of the reticulin network, “unpaired” arteries without bile ducts, sometimes clear or steatotic cells.
Radiological correlation: in an at-risk liver the diagnosis can be made without biopsy (LI-RADS 5) from non-rim arterial phase hyperenhancement, washout in the late phases and the capsule. Unpaired arteries explain the arterialisation; intralesional fat (like the clear cells of this case) causes signal drop on opposed-phase MRI and is an ancillary feature favouring hepatocellular carcinoma.
Nodulo con cellule chiare nel fegato cir: Nodule with clear cells in a cirrhotic liver: hepatocellular carcinoma first; renal metastasis is ruled out with immunohistochemistry.
